component.name: Swift Explorer
component.summary: File manager in the style of the Windows 11 File Explorer

description.p: Swift Explorer looks and behaves like the Windows 11 File Explorer: tabs in the title bar, an address bar with breadcrumbs, a navigation pane and the same keyboard shortcuts.
Folders are read on background threads, so large ones open without freezing the window, and search runs across subfolders in parallel.
A right-click menu for This PC, and the program holding a file is shown when a delete or move fails.

ul.li: Right-clicking This PC in the navigation pane or on its page opens a menu with Open, Open in new tab and Expand.
On Windows, when another program has a file open, a window names that program, can close it and runs the delete or move again once it exits.

description.p: A command palette, split view, batch rename and zip archives.

ul.li: Ctrl+Shift+P opens a command palette that also lists pinned, known and recent folders.
Ctrl+Shift+S shows two folders side by side. F6 switches between them.
F2 with several items selected opens batch rename with a preview and conflict checks.
Zip files can be extracted and created from the right-click menu.
Search results can be narrowed to one file extension, the details pane lists a folder's contents and the status bar shows the git branch.
The default file manager setting keeps working after the app is moved or updated, and --unregister undoes it before uninstalling.

description.p: The app can be the default file manager, and search works on This PC.

ul.li: View has an option to open folders and drives in this app. On Windows Win+E opens it too.
USB drives show up a second after they are plugged in instead of up to 20 seconds later.
On This PC, Enter searches every drive, and typing filters the drive list.
Updates are checked every hour and when the window is reopened. If a new version fails to start twice, the previous one is put back.

description.p: A Properties window on Linux, and a quicker, self-updating Windows version.

ul.li: On Linux, Properties opens the app's own window with General, Security and Details tabs, where permissions and the default app can be changed. It no longer needs a running file manager.
On Windows, closing the window keeps the app waiting in the background, so it opens again right away. It can also start in the background when signing in.
On Windows, new releases are downloaded from GitHub, checked against their SHA-256 and installed automatically.
Menus open without a fade, and the details pane and address bar no longer read the disk on every frame.

description.p: Color schemes, and copies that are safe to unplug when they finish.

ul.li: View > Theme has Catppuccin, Gruvbox, Everforest, Nord, Dracula, Tokyo Night, Rosé Pine and Solarized.
A copy or move finishes only after the files reach the disk, and a message says when the drive can be removed.
Moving to another drive deletes the originals only after that.
On Windows, files can be dragged onto a window that sits on top of Swift Explorer or was brought forward with Alt+Tab.

description.p: Japanese text lines up with Latin letters in file names and labels.

ul.li: German, Spanish, French, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Simplified Chinese and Japanese, picked from the system language or from View > Language.
Chinese, Japanese and Korean file names display with the system's CJK fonts.
The keyboard shortcuts window shows the version and a link to the project page.

description.p: Flatpak package, an install script for Linux, and faster startup.

ul.li: Typing cmd, powershell or terminal in the address bar opens a terminal in the current folder.
Uses the GNOME interface font and shows the right icon on Wayland.
Large folders sort faster, and network drives no longer freeze the window.
